analysis.investment_thesis: Elgi is a genuinely good business — ROIC ~22%, expanding margins, and consistent FCF — but at an EV of ~INR 17,768 Cr against EBIT of INR 529 Cr, the earnings yield is a paltry ~3%, catastrophically far from the Magic Formula's 12%+ threshold. You're paying 42x earnings for a mid-teens revenue grower; the formula says good businesses at bad prices are still bad investments.
key_strengths: ROIC/ROCE of ~22% sustained and expanding — clears the Magic Formula's >20% quality bar
Solid FCF generation: OCF positive all 5 years, FY2025 FCF of INR 298 Cr on INR 529 Cr EBIT (~56% conversion)
Low financial leverage (D/E 0.26) and strong equity build-up from INR 769 Cr (2020) to INR 2,008 Cr (2025)
key_risks: Earnings yield (~3%) is 4x below the Magic Formula's minimum attractive threshold of 12% — the stock is pricing in perfection
FY2023 Other Income of INR 175 Cr (vs. normal INR 14–63 Cr) inflated Net Profit CAGR; underlying earnings power is lower than headline suggests
Revenue growth of 10.7% 9Y CAGR doesn't justify 42x P/E or 32x EV/EBITDA — any margin or growth disappointment compresses the multiple sharply
red_flags: Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = 529/17,768 = ~3% — far below Magic Formula's 12% floor
FY2023 Other Income spike of INR 175 Cr appears one-time; normalized net profit CAGR is materially lower than reported 23.9%
Capex accelerating (INR 95 Cr in FY2025 vs. INR 41 Cr in FY2022) with CWIP jumping to INR 77 Cr — watch for FCF compression
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EV = Market Cap (17,311) + Debt (577) - Cash (120) = INR 17,768 Cr. EBIT (FY2025 Operating Income) = INR 529 Cr. Earnings Yield = 529/17,768 = **2.98%** — catastrophically unattractive. ROIC using Invested Capital (Equity 2,008 + Debt 577 - Cash 120 = 2,465 Cr): 529/2,465 = **21.5%**, corroborated by the reported ROCE of 21.9%. So Elgi scores well on business quality but fails spectacularly on cheapness — exactly the half-good, half-bad case the Magic Formula penalizes.

The underlying business does have merit: margins have expanded structurally (operating margin 9.1% in 2016 → 15.1% in 2025), global diversification in air compressors is real, and FCF is growing. But the market has already priced this story richly at 32x EV/EBITDA. The anomalous FY2023 Other Income (INR 175 Cr) also overstates the earnings CAGR story. At current prices, there is no margin of safety — the Magic Formula would rank Elgi in the bottom decile on earnings yield, making it an automatic avoid regardless of business quality.
